stem: What is the primary function of a Layer 2 switch in an enterprise campus network?
explanation: A Layer 2 switch forwards Ethernet frames using MAC addresses stored in its CAM table. It operates at the Data Link layer and provides microsegmentation by creating separate collision domains for each port. Routers operate at Layer 3 to forward packets between different IP subnets.

choices.text: Forward frames based on destination MAC addresses
Route packets based on destination IP addresses
Perform network address translation between subnets
Filter traffic using stateful inspection rules

stem: Which architectural design combines the distribution and core layers into a single tier?
explanation: A collapsed core design merges the core and distribution layers into a single switch tier. This topology is recommended for smaller enterprise campus networks to reduce hardware costs and operational complexity. Three-tier designs retain dedicated distribution and core switches for larger scalability.

choices.text: Collapsed core topology
Spine-leaf architecture
Three-tier hierarchical model
Hub-and-spoke WAN design

stem: In a modern data center spine-leaf architecture, how do leaf switches connect to the rest of the fabric?
explanation: In a spine-leaf design, every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, but leaf switches never connect to other leaf switches directly. This ensures predictable, consistent low latency across the fabric with equal-cost multipathing (ECMP). Spine switches also do not connect directly to other spine switches.

choices.text: Every leaf connects to every spine switch
Leaves connect directly to adjacent leaf switches
Leaves connect only to a designated primary spine switch
Leaves connect through an access-aggregation ring

stem: Which type of optical fiber is optimized for high-bandwidth transmissions over long distances exceeding 2 kilometers?
explanation: Single-mode fiber (SMF) uses a narrow core (around 9 microns) and a laser light source to transmit signals over long distances with minimal modal dispersion. In contrast, multimode fiber (MMF) has a larger core (50 or 62.5 microns) and is typically used for shorter campus or data center runs under 500 meters.

choices.text: Single-mode fiber (SMF)
Multimode fiber (MMF)
Shielded twisted-pair (STP)
Unshielded twisted-pair (UTP)

stem: What is the default TCP flags sequence during a standard three-way handshake?
explanation: A TCP connection is established using a three-way handshake: the client sends a SYN packet, the server responds with SYN-ACK, and the client finishes the handshake with an ACK packet. After this sequence, reliable bidirectional data transmission can begin.

choices.text: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK
ACK, SYN, ACK
SYN, ACK, FIN
RST, SYN, ACK

stem: How many usable host IP addresses are available in a /28 IPv4 subnet?
explanation: A /28 subnet has 32 - 28 = 4 host bits. The total number of addresses is 2^4 = 16, and subtracting 2 for the network and broadcast addresses leaves 14 usable host addresses.

stem: Which address range is designated for private network addressing under RFC 1918 for Class B networks?
explanation: RFC 1918 reserves 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255 (a /12 block) for private networks in the historical Class B range. The range 10.0.0.0/8 corresponds to Class A, while 192.168.0.0/16 corresponds to Class B private space.

stem: What prefix designates an IPv6 Link-Local address?
explanation: IPv6 link-local addresses always start with the prefix FE80::/10 (typically appearing as fe80::). These addresses are mandatory on all IPv6-enabled interfaces and are used exclusively for communication within the local broadcast domain. They are not routable outside the local link.

stem: Which wireless deployment architecture uses CAPWAP tunnels to split MAC layer processing between an AP and a controller?
explanation: A Split-MAC architecture divides 802.11 processing between the lightweight access point (LAP) and the centralized wireless LAN controller (WLC). Real-time frames like beacons and ACKs are handled by the LAP, while association, authentication, and management are forwarded via CAPWAP to the WLC.

choices.text: Split-MAC architecture with Lightweight APs
Autonomous AP deployment
Ad-hoc peer-to-peer Wi-Fi network
Bridge mode mesh network

stem: What mode allows a Cisco Lightweight AP to locally switch client data traffic if the WAN link to its WLC fails?
explanation: FlexConnect mode (formerly known as H-REAP) enables lightweight access points at branch offices to switch client data frames locally on the local subnet. If connection to the central WLC drops, the AP can continue to provide local connectivity and authentication without interruption.

choices.text: FlexConnect mode
Sniffer mode
Rogue detector mode
Bridge mode

stem: Which field in the IPv4 header prevents packets from endlessly circulating in a routing loop?
explanation: The Time to Live (TTL) field is an 8-bit counter decremented by 1 at every router hop. When the TTL reaches 0, the router drops the packet and sends an ICMP Time Exceeded message back to the sender, preventing permanent routing loops.

choices.text: Time to Live (TTL)
Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP)
Header Checksum
Identification

stem: Which IPv6 header field serves the equivalent role of the IPv4 Time to Live (TTL) field?
explanation: In IPv6, the Hop Limit field is an 8-bit integer decremented by each router that forwards the packet. Just like IPv4 TTL, when the Hop Limit reaches 0, the packet is discarded and an ICMPv6 Hop Limit Exceeded message is returned.

choices.text: Hop Limit
Flow Label
Next Header
Traffic Class

stem: In an EUI-64 IPv6 address generation process, which modifications are made to a 48-bit MAC address?
explanation: To convert a 48-bit MAC address into a 64-bit interface identifier, the 16-bit hex sequence 0xFFFE is inserted into the exact middle of the MAC. Additionally, the 7th bit of the first byte (the universal/local bit) is inverted (flipped).

choices.text: Insert 0xFFFE into the middle and invert the 7th bit
Insert 0xEEEE into the middle and set the 8th bit to 1
Append 0xFFFF to the end and invert the first bit
Prepend 0xFE80 and leave all MAC bits untouched

stem: What is the network address of the subnet containing the host IP 192.168.10.145/27?
explanation: A /27 subnet has a mask of 255.255.255.224, giving a block size of 32 (256 - 224). The subnet boundaries are 0, 32, 64, 96, 128, 160, etc. Since 145 lies between 128 and 159, the network address is 192.168.10.128.

stem: What is the primary characteristic of UDP compared to TCP?
explanation: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol with low overhead. Unlike TCP, UDP does not provide sequencing, acknowledgments, or flow control, making it ideal for delay-sensitive real-time voice and video streams.

choices.text: Connectionless with no guarantee of delivery
Connection-oriented with positive acknowledgments
Provides byte-stream windowing and error retransmissions
Negotiates maximum segment size (MSS) prior to sending

stem: Which connector type is commonly used with Category 6 unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) copper cabling?
explanation: RJ-45 (Registered Jack 45) is the 8-pin modular connector standardized for Ethernet over twisted-pair copper cables like Cat5e, Cat6, and Cat6a. LC, SC, and ST are optical fiber connectors.

choices.text: RJ-45
LC connector
SC connector
BNC connector

stem: What is the broadcast address for the subnet 10.1.4.0/22?
explanation: A /22 mask is 255.255.252.0. The third octet has a block size of 4 (256 - 252). The subnet spans 10.1.4.0 through 10.1.7.255, making 10.1.7.255 the directed broadcast address.

stem: Which wireless frequency band provides more non-overlapping 20 MHz channels to minimize co-channel interference?
explanation: The 5 GHz frequency band offers up to 24 or more non-overlapping 20 MHz channels, depending on regulatory domain and DFS support. By contrast, the 2.4 GHz band provides only three non-overlapping channels (channels 1, 6, and 11 in North America), making it much more susceptible to congestion and co-channel interference.

choices.text: 5 GHz band
2.4 GHz band
900 MHz band
60 GHz band

stem: What is the purpose of the Point-to-Point Protocol over Ethernet (PPPoE) in WAN broadband access?
explanation: PPPoE encapsulates PPP frames inside Ethernet frames, enabling service providers to implement user authentication, session accounting, and link configuration over a shared Ethernet transport like DSL. It allows telcos to manage customer credentials using standard RADIUS or TACACS+ mechanisms.

choices.text: Provide authentication and session management over Ethernet
Establish an encrypted IPsec tunnel over the public internet
Dynamically route BGP prefixes across multiple ISPs
Aggregate multiple physical serial links into a single logical channel

stem: Which IPv4 block is reserved for documentation and examples and must never appear routed on a live network?
explanation: RFC 5737 sets aside three blocks for examples: 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, and 203.0.113.0/24. They are safe to print in diagrams and lab guides precisely because no operator will route them, so a leaked configuration snippet cannot point at real hosts.

stem: Which IPv6 multicast address represents all IPv6 routers on the local link?
explanation: The address FF02::2 is the link-local all-routers multicast address in IPv6. All IPv6 routers listen on this group address for Router Solicitation messages from hosts. FF02::1 represents all IPv6 nodes.

stem: In a three-tier hierarchical network design, what is the primary role of the Core layer?
explanation: The core layer acts as the high-speed network backbone. Its main objective is to switch packets as fast as possible between distribution blocks with low latency and high availability, without performing CPU-intensive tasks like packet filtering or ACL inspection.

choices.text: Provide high-speed, low-latency transport between distribution blocks
Perform granular security filtering and quality of service tagging
Terminate end-user client connections and apply 802.1X security
Distribute IP addresses via DHCP and act as the default gateway

stem: What is the maximum distance supported by standard 1000BASE-T Gigabit Ethernet over Category 5e UTP cabling?
explanation: 1000BASE-T over Cat5e or Cat6 UTP cabling supports a maximum segment length of 100 meters (approximately 328 feet). This includes up to 90 meters of horizontal solid-core cabling and 10 meters of patch cords.

choices.text: 100 meters
50 meters
250 meters
500 meters

stem: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for logical addressing and packet routing across inter-network boundaries?
explanation: The Network layer (Layer 3) handles logical addressing (such as IPv4 and IPv6) and path determination across routed networks. The Data Link layer (Layer 2) handles physical MAC addressing on local segments.

choices.text: Network layer (Layer 3)
Data Link layer (Layer 2)
Transport layer (Layer 4)
Session layer (Layer 5)

stem: What is the function of the Service Set Identifier (SSID) in an 802.11 wireless network?
explanation: An SSID is a human-readable text string (up to 32 characters) that uniquely identifies a specific wireless local area network. Access points broadcast the SSID in 802.11 beacon frames so wireless clients can identify and select the desired wireless network.

choices.text: Identifies the name of the wireless network for clients
Acts as the encryption master key for WPA3 handshakes
Specifies the radio frequency channel allocated to the BSS
Designates the VLAN ID assigned to the AP trunk interface

stem: Which wireless topology feature combines multiple Basic Service Sets (BSSs) connected by a common Distribution System (DS)?
explanation: An Extended Service Set (ESS) consists of two or more interconnected Basic Service Sets (BSSs) sharing the same SSID across a common wired Distribution System. This allows wireless clients to roam seamlessly between access points without dropping their network session.

choices.text: Extended Service Set (ESS)
Independent Basic Service Set (IBSS)
Personal Area Network (PAN)
Mesh Portal Cluster (MPC)

stem: Which encapsulation method is used to transport client traffic between an AP and a central WLC in a unified wireless network?
explanation: Control and Provisioning of Wireless Access Points (CAPWAP) is the standard protocol used between lightweight APs and WLCs. It creates two tunnels: a control tunnel over UDP port 5246 (secured with DTLS) and a data tunnel over UDP port 5247 for client payload frames.

choices.text: CAPWAP data tunnel (UDP 5247)
GRE point-to-point tunnel (IP proto 47)
IPsec transport mode (ESP proto 50)
VXLAN overlay tunnel (UDP 4789)

stem: What is the usable host range for a host configured on network 172.16.80.0/20?
explanation: A /20 subnet has a subnet mask of 255.255.240.0, which has an increment of 16 in the third octet. The network spans 172.16.80.0 through 172.16.95.255. The usable host addresses are 172.16.80.1 through 172.16.95.254.

stem: How many subnets and hosts per subnet are created by subnetting 192.168.1.0/24 with a /29 mask?
explanation: Borrowing from /24 to /29 gives 29 - 24 = 5 borrowed subnet bits, yielding 2^5 = 32 subnets. With 3 host bits remaining (32 - 29 = 3), each subnet has 2^3 - 2 = 6 usable hosts per subnet.

choices.text: 32 subnets with 6 usable hosts each
16 subnets with 14 usable hosts each
64 subnets with 2 usable hosts each
8 subnets with 30 usable hosts each

stem: Which IPv6 address represents the equivalent of IPv4 loopback (127.0.0.1)?
explanation: The IPv6 loopback address is ::1 (or 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 in uncompressed format). It is used by a node to send packets to itself for local testing and internal IPC.

stem: What is the prefix range for IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (ULA) specified in RFC 4193?
explanation: Unique Local Addresses use the block FC00::/7 (which encompasses FC00::/8 and FD00::/8). They are analogous to IPv4 RFC 1918 private addresses and are meant for local routing within an organization without being routed over the public internet.

stem: Which transceiver form-factor supports 40 Gigabit Ethernet connections over fiber or DAC cabling?
explanation: QSFP+ (Quad Small Form-factor Pluggable Plus) is the compact, hot-swappable transceiver standard designed for 40 Gbps data links by bundling four 10 Gbps lanes. SFP supports 1 Gbps, and SFP+ supports 10 Gbps.

choices.text: QSFP+
SFP+
GBIC
XFP

stem: Which field in the TCP header is used by the receiver to inform the sender how many bytes of data it can accept before receiving an acknowledgment?
explanation: The Window Size field in the TCP header dictates the receive window (rwnd). This is the core mechanism of TCP flow control, preventing a fast sender from overwhelming a receiver's buffer space.

choices.text: Window Size
Sequence Number
Acknowledgment Number
Urgent Pointer

stem: Which WAN topology offers the highest redundancy and fault tolerance at the highest implementation cost?
explanation: A full mesh topology connects every site directly to every other site with dedicated circuits. While it provides zero single points of failure and optimal path routing, the circuit count grows exponentially with n*(n-1)/2, making it the most expensive WAN design.

choices.text: Full mesh topology
Hub-and-spoke topology
Partial mesh topology
Point-to-point leased line

stem: In a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW), what capability distinguishes it from a traditional stateful inspection firewall?
explanation: A Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) integrates deep packet inspection, application awareness (identifying applications regardless of port), and built-in intrusion prevention systems (IPS). Traditional stateful firewalls inspect only Layer 3 and Layer 4 header attributes like IP addresses and TCP/UDP ports.

choices.text: Application-level inspection and integrated IPS
Stateful tracking of TCP SYN/ACK flags
Basic Layer 4 port filtering
Static NAT address translation

stem: Which standard defines 802.11ax wireless technology, commonly known as Wi-Fi 6?
explanation: IEEE 802.11ax is branded by the Wi-Fi Alliance as Wi-Fi 6. It introduces Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiple Access (OFDMA), Target Wake Time (TWT), and 1024-QAM to dramatically increase network efficiency and client density in congested environments.

choices.text: Wi-Fi 6E (802.11be)

stem: What feature in Wi-Fi 6 allows multiple clients with different bandwidth requirements to transmit simultaneously on the same channel?
explanation: OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiple Access) subdivides a single Wi-Fi channel into smaller frequency allocations called Resource Units (RUs). This allows the access point to communicate with multiple clients in parallel in both uplink and downlink, drastically cutting latency.

choices.text: OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiple Access)
CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance)
MIMO beamforming arrays
Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS)

stem: Which parameter is dynamically negotiated using TCP MSS (Maximum Segment Size)?
explanation: The TCP MSS dictates the maximum amount of payload data (excluding IP and TCP headers) that a host can receive in a single TCP segment. During the initial three-way handshake, each host advertises its MSS, which is typically derived from the interface MTU minus 40 bytes (for IPv4).

choices.text: The maximum payload data size in a single TCP segment
The total size of the Ethernet frame including preamble
The maximum number of TCP segments sent without an ACK
The maximum allowable transmission delay across a WAN link

stem: Which IPv4 header field is recalculated by every router that forwards a packet?
explanation: The Header Checksum covers only the IPv4 header, and because the TTL is decremented at each hop the checksum must be recomputed each time. A router that receives a packet whose header checksum does not match discards it.

choices.text: Header Checksum
Identification
Total Length
Protocol

stem: Which IPv4 header fields work together so that fragments can be reassembled in the correct order?
explanation: The Identification field tags all fragments belonging to the same original datagram, while the Fragment Offset records where each fragment's payload belongs. The More Fragments flag marks all but the last fragment.

choices.text: Identification and Fragment Offset
TTL and Protocol
Version and IHL
Source and Destination Address

stem: What is the minimum size of an IPv4 header when no options are present?
explanation: The fixed portion of the IPv4 header is 20 bytes. The IHL field expresses the header length in 32-bit words, so a value of 5 means 20 bytes; options can extend it to a maximum of 60 bytes.

choices.text: 20 bytes
8 bytes
14 bytes
40 bytes

stem: What is the fixed size of the base IPv6 header?
explanation: The IPv6 base header is a fixed 40 bytes. Optional features are moved into extension headers chained through the Next Header field, which is why the base header never changes size.

choices.text: 40 bytes
20 bytes
24 bytes
60 bytes

stem: Which IPv6 header field can label a traffic flow for special handling without inspecting the transport header?
explanation: The 20-bit Flow Label identifies packets that belong to the same flow so routers can apply consistent treatment without parsing upper-layer headers. A value of zero means the packet has not been assigned to any flow.

choices.text: Flow Label
Traffic Class
Next Header
Payload Length

stem: What does the Next Header field in an IPv6 packet identify?
explanation: Next Header points to whatever follows the current header: an upper-layer protocol such as TCP or UDP, or another extension header. This chaining is how IPv6 adds optional behavior without growing the base header.

choices.text: The header or upper-layer protocol that follows the current header
The IPv6 address of the next-hop router toward the destination
The maximum payload size the source is willing to send
The number of routers the packet has already traversed

stem: Which OSI layer is responsible for formatting, compression, and encryption of data?
explanation: The Presentation layer handles how data is represented to the application, including character encoding, compression, and encryption. It sits between the Application layer and the Session layer.

choices.text: Presentation
Session
Transport
Data Link

stem: At which OSI layer are MAC addresses used to deliver frames on a local segment?
explanation: Layer 2, the Data Link layer, uses MAC addresses to deliver frames between devices on the same broadcast domain. Layer 3 then uses IP addresses to move packets between networks.

choices.text: Data Link
Network
Transport
Physical

stem: Which device forwards traffic between different IP networks by choosing a next hop from a routing table?
explanation: A router examines the destination IP address, consults its routing table, and forwards the packet toward the best matching next hop. This is what separates broadcast domains and connects distinct subnets.

choices.text: Router
Layer 2 switch
Hub
Access point

stem: What is the function of a wireless access point in an enterprise LAN?
explanation: An AP bridges wireless clients onto the wired LAN, typically by mapping each SSID to a VLAN and tagging frames toward the wired uplink. In a controller-based design the AP is often a lightweight device managed centrally.

choices.text: It bridges wireless clients onto the wired LAN
It assigns public IP addresses to wireless clients using NAT
It provides Layer 3 routing between wireless subnets
It stores the MAC address table for the entire campus

stem: What is the primary function of a firewall between network zones?
explanation: A firewall enforces an access policy on traffic crossing between zones, permitting or denying flows based on addresses, ports, application, or state. It is placed at trust boundaries rather than inside a single flat segment.

choices.text: It permits or denies traffic between zones according to a configured policy
It converts private addresses to public addresses for every host
It learns MAC addresses and forwards frames within a VLAN
It distributes routing updates between autonomous systems

stem: Why are publicly reachable servers placed in a DMZ rather than on the internal LAN?
explanation: A DMZ is a segment isolated from the internal network by the firewall, so a compromised public server cannot reach internal hosts directly. Traffic from the DMZ to the inside is restricted to only what the service truly needs.

choices.text: It isolates internet-facing servers so a compromise cannot reach internal hosts directly
It guarantees higher bandwidth for public web traffic
It removes the need for any access control lists on the firewall
It automatically encrypts all traffic destined for the internet

stem: In a spine-leaf data center fabric, why is every leaf connected to every spine?
explanation: A full mesh between leaves and spines gives any two leaves an equal-cost path of exactly two hops. This produces predictable latency and lets routing protocols use all links simultaneously instead of blocking redundant ones.

choices.text: It gives predictable two-hop paths and lets every link be used simultaneously
It allows spanning tree to block the redundant links for loop prevention
It removes the need for any Layer 3 routing in the data center
It ensures each leaf has a single path to the core for simplicity

stem: In a spine-leaf fabric, why are spines not connected to each other?
explanation: Spines act only as a high-speed transit tier between leaves. Connecting spines to each other would add hops and create the potential for loops without improving any leaf-to-leaf path.

choices.text: Spines are pure transit devices, and interconnecting them would add hops and possible loops
Spines have no routing table and therefore cannot form adjacencies
Spine ports are reserved exclusively for out-of-band management
Spine-to-spine links would collapse the VXLAN overlay

stem: In a three-tier campus design, which layer aggregates access switches and enforces routing and security policy?
explanation: The distribution layer sits between access and core. It terminates access VLANs, runs inter-VLAN routing, applies ACLs and QoS policy, and summarizes routes toward the core so the core can stay simple and fast.

choices.text: The distribution layer
The access layer
The core layer
The data center layer

stem: What is the role of the access layer in a Cisco campus architecture?
explanation: The access layer is the edge that end devices physically attach to. It provides port density, PoE, VLAN assignment, port security, and 802.1X authentication before traffic is handed upward.

choices.text: Connecting end devices and applying port-level services such as PoE, VLANs, and port security
Providing high-speed transit between distribution blocks
Hosting the default gateway for every VLAN in the campus
Terminating WAN circuits from the service provider

stem: Which IPv4 address range is reserved for loopback testing and is never forwarded by a router?
explanation: The 127.0.0.0/8 range is reserved for loopback. An address such as 127.0.0.1 refers to the local TCP/IP stack, and packets sent to this range are never placed on a physical link or forwarded by a router.

stem: What is the broadcast address of the subnet 192.168.10.64/26?
explanation: A /26 has a block size of 64, so the subnets start at .0, .64, .128 and .192. The .64 subnet spans 192.168.10.64 through 192.168.10.127, and the last address in that range is the broadcast.

stem: Which WAN topology connects every remote site to one central hub, forcing spoke-to-spoke traffic to transit the hub?
explanation: A hub-and-spoke WAN is cheap to build because each site needs only one circuit, but it creates a single point of failure and adds latency for site-to-site traffic. A full mesh or DMVPN removes that hairpin at higher cost or complexity.

choices.text: Hub-and-spoke
Full mesh
Point-to-point
Ring

stem: Which WAN service provides any-to-any connectivity through the provider cloud without the customer building a full mesh of physical circuits?
explanation: An MPLS VPN lets the provider label and forward customer traffic across a shared backbone, so every site needs only one link to the provider while still reaching every other site. The customer sees a private, any-to-any network without owning the mesh.

choices.text: MPLS VPN
Leased line
Dark fiber
Metro Ethernet E-Line

stem: Which 802.11 amendment introduced the 5 GHz band with a maximum data rate of 54 Mbps?
explanation: 802.11a was the first 5 GHz OFDM standard and reached 54 Mbps. 802.11b stayed on 2.4 GHz at 11 Mbps, 802.11g brought 54 Mbps to 2.4 GHz, and 802.11n added MIMO on both bands.

stem: What is the widest channel supported by 802.11ac?
explanation: 802.11ac introduced 80 MHz channels and an optional 160 MHz mode (or 80+80 MHz on two non-contiguous segments). Wider channels raise throughput but consume more of the band, so dense deployments usually stay at 20 or 40 MHz.

choices.text: 160 MHz
20 MHz
40 MHz
80 MHz

stem: What is the primary function of a multilayer (Layer 3) switch in a campus network?
explanation: A multilayer switch forwards at Layer 2 within a VLAN and routes between VLANs in hardware, so the default gateway for each subnet lives on the switch itself instead of on an external router.

choices.text: Switching within VLANs and routing between them at wire speed
Extending a VLAN across a WAN link
Converting broadcast domains into collision domains
Providing PoE only to IP phones

stem: Which OSI layer provides reliable end-to-end delivery using sequencing, acknowledgments and flow control?
explanation: The transport layer (Layer 4) is where TCP establishes a session, numbers segments so they can be reassembled, acknowledges receipt, and slows down when the receiver cannot keep up. Layer 3 delivers packets between networks but makes no delivery guarantee.

choices.text: The transport layer (Layer 4)
The network layer (Layer 3)
The data link layer (Layer 2)
The session layer (Layer 5)

stem: How does an intrusion prevention system (IPS) differ from an intrusion detection system (IDS)?
explanation: Both inspect traffic against signatures and behavioral rules, but an IDS receives a copy of the traffic and can only alert. An IPS sits inline in the forwarding path, so it can drop or reset a malicious flow before it reaches the target.

choices.text: An IPS is inline and can block traffic; an IDS only monitors a copy and alerts
An IPS works only on encrypted traffic; an IDS works only on cleartext
An IPS protects endpoints; an IDS protects network devices
An IPS requires a TAP; an IDS requires a firewall

stem: Why is a spine-leaf fabric preferred over a traditional three-tier design for data center east-west traffic?
explanation: Every leaf is one hop from every spine, so any server-to-server path has the same predictable latency and the fabric can be scaled by adding leaves or spines. Three-tier designs add aggregation hops and oversubscribe the uplinks where most server traffic must cross.

choices.text: Every leaf-to-leaf path is the same short hop count, giving predictable latency and easy horizontal scaling
It eliminates the need for Layer 3 routing inside the data center
It removes the need for redundant links between switches
It concentrates all traffic through a single core pair

stem: What does a Wireless LAN Controller provide to lightweight access points in a centralized deployment?
explanation: The WLC centralizes configuration, RF channel and power planning, client authentication, roaming decisions and firmware for every joined AP. The AP keeps only the real-time MAC functions, which is why the split is called split-MAC.

choices.text: Centralized configuration, RF management, client authentication and roaming for all joined APs
Local switching of all client traffic without a tunnel
Layer 2 trunking between access switches
DHCP and DNS services for wireless clients

stem: What does a Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID) identify?
explanation: The BSSID is the MAC address of a single AP radio in a basic service set. Several BSSIDs can carry the same SSID to form an extended service set, which is how clients see one network name across many access points.

choices.text: A single access point radio within one basic service set
The network name that clients select when associating
The group of APs sharing one distribution system
The encryption key used by the basic service set

stem: How many total addresses does a /26 block contain, including the network and broadcast addresses?
explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits, so the block contains 2^6 = 64 addresses. Two of them are reserved for the network and broadcast addresses, leaving 62 usable host addresses. Counting total instead of usable addresses is a common off-by-two error.

stem: Why do large data-center fabrics use ECMP across spine links in a spine-leaf topology?
explanation: Every leaf peers with every spine, creating multiple equal-cost paths. ECMP hashes individual flows across those paths so aggregate east-west bandwidth scales with the number of spines, without reconfiguring the leaves or relying on STP.

choices.text: To spread flows across multiple equal-cost spine paths and scale bandwidth
To elect a single active spine and block the rest, avoiding loops
To replace routing protocols with Spanning Tree on the leaf uplinks
To guarantee that all traffic from one host follows the same spine

stem: Which TCP flag instructs the receiving host to hand buffered data to the application immediately instead of waiting for more segments?
explanation: Set on the last segment of an interactive write, PSH tells the receiver's stack to flush what it has buffered upward rather than batching it. Applications that send a short request and then wait for a reply depend on that prompt delivery, otherwise the stalled data waits for a full buffer.

choices.text: PSH
URG
SYN
FIN

stem: A hypervisor that runs directly on the server hardware without an underlying host operating system is best described as which type?
explanation: Type 1 hypervisors such as ESXi and Hyper-V run bare-metal on the hardware and own the drivers directly. Type 2 hypervisors such as VirtualBox and VMware Workstation run as an application on top of a conventional host OS. Type 1 is the usual choice for data center virtualization because it removes the host OS from the performance and patching path.

choices.text: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor
Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor
Container runtime
Overlay network gateway

stem: What is the key architectural difference between a virtual machine and a container?
explanation: Each virtual machine carries its own complete guest operating system and kernel, so the hypervisor must virtualize hardware for every instance. Containers share the host kernel and isolate only the process, filesystem, and network namespace. That shared kernel is why containers start in milliseconds and are far denser than VMs, at the cost of weaker isolation.

choices.text: A VM includes its own guest OS and kernel; a container shares the host kernel
A container includes its own guest OS and kernel; a VM shares the host kernel
A VM cannot have an IP address, while every container must have one
A container requires a physical network adapter, while a VM does not

stem: Two virtual machines on the same hypervisor host exchange frames through a virtual switch. Which statement describes how that traffic is handled?
explanation: A virtual switch forwards frames between virtual NICs in software on the hypervisor, so same-host traffic never needs a physical adapter or an external switch. The frames only traverse a physical uplink when the destination sits outside the host and the port group is bound to an uplink. This is why same-host VM-to-VM throughput can exceed the speed of the physical NIC.

choices.text: It is switched in software on the host and stays local unless the destination is external
It is always flooded out the physical uplink before reaching the peer VM
It must be routed by the physical top-of-rack switch in every case
It is dropped because two VMs cannot share a broadcast domain

stem: Which field in a VXLAN header identifies the individual Layer 2 segment that a frame belongs to?
explanation: VXLAN places a 24-bit VNI in its header to identify the tenant or Layer 2 segment, which allows roughly 16 million segments compared with the 4094 VLAN IDs of 802.1Q. The original Ethernet frame is encapsulated inside UDP, normally destination port 4789. The VNI is what lets the same VLAN ID be reused by many isolated tenants on shared physical infrastructure.

choices.text: The 24-bit VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI)
The 12-bit 802.1Q VLAN Identifier
The 8-bit IP Time To Live field
The 16-bit UDP source port

stem: A laptop's Ethernet adapter shows a link light but the host has been assigned the address 169.254.37.12. What does this address indicate?
explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the IPv4 link-local range that a host self-assigns when DHCP fails, commonly called APIPA. The link light only proves the physical and data-link layers are up; it says nothing about whether a DHCP server was reachable. The investigator should check VLAN assignment, relay configuration, and DHCP scope exhaustion rather than the cable.

choices.text: The host could not reach a DHCP server and self-assigned a link-local address
The host received a valid address from a DHCP server on the local subnet
The Ethernet cable is faulty and no frames can be transmitted
The host is using a statically configured public address

stem: A user can successfully ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot open www.example.com. Which cause is most likely?
explanation: Reaching an external IP address proves the local link, default gateway, and internet routing all work. Name resolution is the only remaining step that differs between the two tests, so a failed or unreachable DNS server is the prime suspect. Verifying the configured resolver with a direct query confirms it quickly.

choices.text: Name resolution is failing or the configured DNS server is unreachable
The default gateway is misconfigured or missing
The Ethernet duplex setting is mismatched
The host has an APIPA address

stem: A workstation can reach every host in its own subnet but nothing beyond it. Which configuration should be checked first?
explanation: Intra-subnet delivery uses ARP and Layer 2 forwarding only, while every off-subnet destination requires the host to send to its default gateway. A host with a wrong or missing default gateway therefore behaves exactly this way. The subnet mask is worth confirming too, since an overly wide mask makes remote hosts look local.

choices.text: The default gateway address and the subnet mask
The DNS search domain suffix
The duplex and speed settings of the switch port
The MTU size configured on the NIC

stem: A wireless client associates successfully but drops connections intermittently while far from the access point. Which action addresses the most likely cause?
explanation: A client that associates but disconnects intermittently at range is usually suffering weak signal and high retransmission, not an addressing problem. Improving coverage by relocating or adding an access point, or tuning channel and transmit power, attacks the root cause. Changing IP settings or DNS would not affect radio-layer stability.

choices.text: Improve radio coverage by relocating or adding an access point and adjusting channel and power
Assign the client a static IP address in the correct VLAN
Change the client's DNS servers to a public resolver
Disable DHCP snooping on the client's VLAN

stem: An enterprise needs an encrypted connection from its on-premises router to a cloud virtual network across the public internet. Which option fits?
explanation: A site-to-site IPsec VPN builds encrypted tunnels over any internet path between the on-premises gateway and the cloud VPN gateway. It needs no dedicated circuit and is the standard low-cost way to connect a branch or data center to a cloud VPC. A dedicated interconnect would bypass the internet entirely rather than encrypt a path across it.

choices.text: A site-to-site IPsec VPN between the on-premises router and the cloud VPN gateway
A dedicated private circuit from a carrier that bypasses the internet
A public DNS zone hosted by the cloud provider
A Layer 2 trunk extended from the data center over the internet

stem: Which connectivity option provides a private, dedicated circuit between an enterprise data center and a cloud provider without traversing the public internet?
explanation: Dedicated interconnects such as AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute give a private physical or carrier-provided path into the provider's network. Because the traffic bypasses the public internet, these links offer more predictable latency and bandwidth than a VPN over broadband. They are more expensive and take longer to provision than an internet VPN.

choices.text: A dedicated private interconnect such as Direct Connect or ExpressRoute
A site-to-site IPsec tunnel over a broadband internet connection
A remote-access VPN terminated on a cloud host
A client-to-site SSL portal

stem: Instances in a cloud private subnet need outbound internet access for software updates but must not accept inbound connections from the internet. Which component provides this?
explanation: A NAT gateway performs source NAT for traffic leaving the private subnet, so replies return to the gateway and are forwarded back to the instance. Because no inbound mapping exists, internet hosts cannot initiate a session to those instances. Assigning public IPs or opening the security group inbound would defeat the requirement.

choices.text: A NAT gateway attached to the private subnet's route table
A public IP address assigned directly to each instance
An inbound security group rule permitting all sources
A virtual private gateway terminating an IPsec tunnel

stem: What does a cloud provider's virtual private gateway terminate in a hybrid cloud design?
explanation: The virtual private gateway is the provider-side endpoint of the tunnels that connect a virtual network to an on-premises gateway. The customer-side device is the customer gateway, and the two ends form the site-to-site VPN. Route tables then direct traffic for on-premises prefixes into that gateway.

choices.text: The VPN tunnels that connect the cloud virtual network to the on-premises gateway
The DNS zone that publishes the cloud application
The load balancer that distributes traffic across instances
The object storage bucket that holds virtual machine images

stem: Which IEEE standard defines 1000BASE-T over twisted-pair copper?
explanation: Gigabit Ethernet over Category 5e arrived as 802.3ab, using all four pairs in both directions at once. The earlier 802.3z covered the fiber variants, and 802.3af is the Power over Ethernet amendment, so neither describes the copper gigabit PHY.

stem: Which copper cabling category is rated for 10GBASE-T across the full 100-meter channel?
explanation: Category 6a is specified for 10GBASE-T at 100 meters and adds shielding or improved construction to control alien crosstalk. Category 6 can carry 10GBASE-T only up to about 55 meters, and Category 5e is not rated for 10 Gbps at all. For full-length 10-gigabit copper runs, 6a is the minimum.

choices.text: Category 6a
Category 6
Category 5e
Category 3

stem: How far can 10GBASE-SR travel over OM3 laser-optimized multimode fiber?
explanation: OM3 is rated for 300 meters at 10 Gbps with short-reach optics, and OM4 raises that to 400 meters. Beyond those distances the modal dispersion of multimode fiber forces a move to single-mode, which is why campus backbones typically switch to single-mode past a few hundred meters.

choices.text: 300 meters
100 meters
550 meters
10 kilometers

stem: A twisted-pair cable is terminated with T568A on one end and T568B on the other. What is this cable?
explanation: A straight-through cable uses the same pinout at both ends, while a crossover cable deliberately wires one end to T568A and the other to T568B so the transmit pair at one end lands on the receive pair at the other. It was used to link like devices such as switch-to-switch. Modern ports implement auto-MDIX, so either cable type now works in most cases.

choices.text: A crossover cable, historically used between like devices
A straight-through cable, used between unlike devices
A rollover cable, used for console access
A fiber patch cord with mismatched connectors

stem: A cable must be installed in the return-air space above a suspended ceiling. Which cable rating is required for that location?
explanation: A plenum space moves building air, so a fire there would distribute smoke and toxic gas through the whole floor. CMP cable uses a low-smoke, low-flame-spread jacket. CMR is for risers between floors, CMG for general in-wall runs, and CMX for outdoor exposure.

choices.text: CMP (plenum-rated)
CMR (riser-rated)
CMG (general-purpose)
CMX (outdoor-rated)

stem: What is the primary purpose of the metallic shield in a shielded twisted-pair (STP) cable?
explanation: The foil or braid acts as a barrier: interference induces a current in the shield, which is bonded to ground and taken out of the signal path. The pairs must stay twisted and balanced, and the shield does not carry signal return current.

choices.text: It drains induced electromagnetic interference to ground before it couples onto the pairs
It increases the cable's tensile strength for long pulls
It carries the signal return path for each pair
It prevents the pairs from untwisting inside the jacket

stem: Which Ethernet standard allows 2.5 Gbps over existing Category 5e cabling, typically to uplink a Wi-Fi 6 access point?
explanation: IEEE 802.3bz defined 2.5GBASE-T and 5GBASE-T so installed Cat 5e and Cat 6 runs could carry more than 1 Gbps without recabling. It is the usual choice when an access point can exceed a Gigabit uplink but the cable plant will not support 10GBASE-T.

choices.text: 2.5GBASE-T (IEEE 802.3bz)
1000BASE-T (IEEE 802.3ab)
10GBASE-T (IEEE 802.3an)
40GBASE-T (IEEE 802.3bq)

stem: A cable tester reports that pairs 1-2 and 3-6 pass, while pairs 4-5 and 7-8 are open. What does this indicate?
explanation: 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX use only pairs 1-2 and 3-6. 1000BASE-T and faster use all four pairs, so an open on 4-5 or 7-8 lets the link come up at 100 Mbps and fail Gigabit autonegotiation. A tester that reports per-pair continuity localises the fault to the termination.

choices.text: Two pairs are broken or mis-pinned, so the link can run 10/100 but not Gigabit
The cable is a working crossover cable
The cable is shielded and needs a ground bond
The link is running at full duplex but half speed

stem: Why are the parallel links between an access switch and its distribution switch usually bundled into an EtherChannel?
explanation: Spanning tree blocks redundant parallel links to prevent loops, which wastes half the capacity. An EtherChannel is presented to STP as one port, so all members can forward at once and the bundle's throughput is the sum of its members.

choices.text: The bundle adds bandwidth while spanning tree sees a single logical link
The bundle lets each VLAN use a different physical link without STP
The bundle makes the access switch the spanning-tree root
The bundle carries only voice traffic and leaves data on one link

stem: In the Cisco enterprise campus architecture, what is the function of the services block?
explanation: The services block holds the servers that every other block depends on: DNS, DHCP, NTP, AAA, and management tools. Keeping them in one module makes them easier to secure and to scale independently of the access and core layers.

choices.text: It centralises shared services such as DNS, DHCP, NTP, and AAA for the campus
It terminates the ISP circuits at the internet edge
It aggregates the building distribution switches
It provides the wireless client access layer

stem: What is a building block (pod) in a modular campus design?
explanation: Modular designs replicate a proven access-plus-distribution unit for each building or floor. Because every pod follows the same template, capacity can be added one pod at a time and a fault inside one pod stays local instead of affecting the whole campus.

choices.text: A repeatable group of access and distribution switches deployed per building or floor
The redundant pair of core switches at the centre of the campus
A single wiring closet with one access switch
The DMZ segment that faces the internet

stem: What is the main benefit of making the access-to-distribution uplink a routed Layer 3 link instead of a Layer 2 trunk?
explanation: A routed uplink ends the Layer 2 domain at the access switch. With no loop in that segment, spanning tree does not need to block the redundant path, and equal-cost routing can use both links. VLANs stay local, which also shrinks failure domains.

choices.text: Both uplinks can forward at once because there is no Layer 2 loop for spanning tree to block
It lets every VLAN extend across the entire campus
It removes the need for an interior gateway protocol
It doubles the number of broadcast domains on the access switch

stem: A desktop's Ethernet port shows no link light after the cable is connected. Which layer should be checked first?
explanation: A missing link light means the two PHYs never established a physical connection, so nothing above Layer 1 can work. Reseat or swap the cable, try another wall jack, and check that the switch port is not shut down or err-disabled before looking at addressing.

choices.text: Layer 1: the cable, the wall jack, the switch port, and the NIC
Layer 3: the default gateway address
Layer 4: the TCP port the application uses
Layer 7: the DNS server configuration

stem: A server answers on TCP 22 and TCP 443 but connections to TCP 3306 time out. Which cause best fits?
explanation: If other services on the same host respond, the path, addressing, and name resolution are working. A single port that silently times out points to a filter, such as a firewall policy or an ACL, that permits the other ports but not this one.

choices.text: A firewall or ACL is dropping traffic for that specific port
The default gateway is missing on the server
DNS resolution is failing for the server name
The Ethernet cable is damaged

stem: A switch interface shows a steadily rising count of CRC and input errors. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: CRC errors mean the frame arrived with a bad checksum, which is a physical or link problem: a crushed cable, a dirty or poorly crimped connector, or a duplex mismatch. IP and MAC address issues show up as reachability or flooding problems, not checksum failures.

choices.text: A damaged cable, bad connector, or duplex mismatch corrupting frames in transit
An IP address conflict on the VLAN
A missing default route on the switch
A duplicate MAC address in the CAM table

stem: Two hosts on the same VLAN are manually configured with the same IPv4 address. What symptom typically appears?
explanation: Both hosts answer ARP for the same address, so neighbours cache whichever MAC replied last and traffic alternates between the two machines. Connections reset or stall unpredictably. A DHCP-managed address plan, or DHCP snooping and DAI, prevents the conflict.

choices.text: Intermittent connectivity and ARP conflicts as each host claims the address
Both hosts lose link light on their switch ports
The switch shuts down the entire VLAN
DNS stops resolving for every host on the VLAN

stem: In a cloud VPC, what determines whether a subnet's traffic goes to an internet gateway, a NAT gateway, or a peered VPC?
explanation: Subnets are associated with a route table, and the longest matching route decides the next hop. Security groups filter whether traffic is allowed, but they do not choose the path. A subnet with no route to an internet gateway stays private even if its security group permits outbound traffic.

choices.text: The route table associated with the subnet
The MAC address of the instance's virtual NIC
The outbound rules in the security group
The TTL value in the instance's DNS resolver

stem: Two VPCs must exchange traffic over private IP addresses without a VPN or a gateway appliance. Which feature provides that?
explanation: VPC peering creates a direct private route between two VPCs, so instances talk using their private addresses and traffic does not leave the provider's network. It is not transitive: if A peers with B and B peers with C, A still cannot reach C without its own peering or a transit gateway.

choices.text: VPC peering
An internet gateway
A NAT gateway
A site-to-site VPN connection

stem: An enterprise has dozens of VPCs plus on-premises connections that must all reach each other. Which component replaces a full mesh of peerings with one hub?
explanation: A transit gateway is a regional hub that VPCs and on-premises links attach to, so each network needs one attachment instead of a peering to every other network. That removes the growth of peerings with each new VPC and gives one place to apply routing and segmentation policy.

choices.text: A transit gateway
A NAT instance in every VPC
A public-facing load balancer
An internet gateway per VPC

stem: What does a cloud load balancer do for an application tier that runs on several instances?
explanation: The load balancer holds the client-facing address and distributes connections across a target group. Health checks remove an instance that stops responding, so capacity and availability survive a single instance failure. Encryption and addressing are handled by other services.

choices.text: It spreads incoming requests across healthy targets and stops sending traffic to failed ones
It assigns private IP addresses to the instances
It encrypts traffic between the application instances
It stores the application's session database

stem: Which IPv4 address is the limited broadcast address, which is never forwarded beyond the local link?
explanation: 255.255.255.255 means every host on this link, and routers do not forward it. A directed broadcast such as 192.168.1.255 targets all hosts in one subnet and can be routed if the router is configured to allow it. 224.0.0.1 is the all-hosts multicast group, and 127.0.0.1 is loopback.

stem: Which IPv4 address range is reserved for multicast group addresses?
explanation: Class D space, 224.0.0.0/4, is used for multicast groups, with 224.0.0.0/24 reserved for link-local control traffic such as OSPF and EIGRP hellos. 169.254.0.0/16 is APIPA, 172.16.0.0/12 is RFC 1918 private space, and 100.64.0.0/10 is carrier-grade NAT space.

stem: Which address block is reserved for carrier-grade NAT by RFC 6598 and should not be used for enterprise private addressing?
explanation: RFC 6598 sets aside 100.64.0.0/10 as the shared address space that a carrier uses between its CGNAT platform and customer edge devices. It is not one of the RFC 1918 private ranges, so an enterprise that also uses it can collide with the carrier's addressing.

stem: What does a subnet mask tell an IPv4 host?
explanation: The mask marks the boundary between the network prefix and the host portion. The host ANDs its address with the mask to learn its own subnet, then compares a destination's masked address to decide whether to send directly or to the default gateway.

choices.text: Which bits of the address identify the network and which identify the host
Which default gateway the host should use
Which DNS server the host should query first
Which VLAN the host's switch port belongs to

stem: Which IPv4 header field tells the destination host which upper-layer protocol should receive the payload?
explanation: The Protocol field carries a number such as 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP, or 1 for ICMP. The receiving host uses it to hand the payload to the correct transport or control module. Version identifies IPv4 itself, and Total Length covers the whole packet.

choices.text: Protocol
Version
Total Length
Header Checksum

stem: Which IPv4 header field is used to mark packets so routers can apply QoS treatment?
explanation: The DS field, formerly the Type of Service byte, holds the 6-bit Differentiated Services Code Point. A router reads the DSCP to choose a per-hop behaviour, such as expedited forwarding for voice. The other fields support fragmentation and reassembly.

choices.text: The Differentiated Services field, which carries the DSCP value
The Identification field
The Flags field
The Fragment Offset field

stem: An IPv4 packet carries options, so its header is longer than 20 bytes. Which field tells a router where the header ends and the payload begins?
explanation: IHL counts 32-bit words in the header, so a value of 6 means 24 bytes and the payload starts there. Total Length measures the whole packet, not the header boundary. Without IHL a router could not parse a variable-length header.

choices.text: Internet Header Length (IHL)
Total Length
Fragment Offset
Header Checksum

stem: A router drops an oversized packet because the Don't Fragment (DF) bit is set and returns an ICMP fragmentation-needed message. What should the sender do?
explanation: Path MTU discovery relies on that ICMP message: the source learns the smallest MTU on the path and shrinks its payload to fit, so no router has to fragment. Clearing DF would let routers fragment, which is exactly what the application was trying to avoid.

choices.text: Reduce its segment size to the reported MTU and continue using path MTU discovery
Clear the DF bit and resend without changing the size
Increase the TTL so the packet survives the path
Recalculate the header checksum and resend the same packet

stem: Why does the IPv6 header have no header checksum?
explanation: Every router used to decrement the TTL and recompute the IPv4 header checksum, which costs forwarding capacity. IPv6 assumes the link layer or a transport checksum detects bit errors, so it drops the field and lets routers forward with less work.

choices.text: Link-layer and upper-layer checksums already catch corruption, so the per-hop recalculation was removed to speed forwarding
IPv6 relies on the Hop Limit field to detect corrupted headers
The checksum was moved into the extension headers
IPv6 packets cannot be corrupted in transit

stem: Which IPv6 header field plays the role that the IPv4 DSCP field plays for QoS?
explanation: The 8-bit Traffic Class field carries the DSCP marking, so an IPv6 router can classify and queue a packet the same way it would an IPv4 packet. Flow Label is a separate 20-bit field used to identify a flow for special handling.

choices.text: Traffic Class
Flow Label
Payload Length
Next Header

stem: What does the Payload Length field in the IPv6 header count?
explanation: IPv6 puts the fixed 40-byte base header outside the count, so Payload Length covers extension headers and the upper-layer payload together. That differs from the IPv4 Total Length field, which measures the entire packet including its header.

choices.text: Everything after the 40-byte base header, including any extension headers
Only the TCP or UDP segment
The base header plus the payload
The number of extension headers in the packet

stem: In IPv6, which device is permitted to fragment a packet?
explanation: IPv6 removed router fragmentation. A router that cannot forward an oversized packet sends an ICMPv6 Packet Too Big message, and the source then fragments with a Fragment extension header or reduces its payload. That keeps routers fast and pushes the work to the endpoints.

choices.text: Only the source host, using a Fragment extension header
Any router whose egress MTU is smaller than the packet
Only the last router before the destination
Any device that lowers the path MTU

stem: Replacing a hub with a switch on the same segment changes which property?
explanation: A hub repeats every bit out of every port, so all attached devices share one collision domain and one bandwidth pool. A switch stores and forwards frames per port, so each port is its own collision domain while the broadcast domain stays the same size.

choices.text: Each switch port becomes its own collision domain
The broadcast domain shrinks to a single port
The segment gains a routing table
All ports continue to share one collision domain

stem: What is the purpose of a media converter?
explanation: A media converter changes the electrical or optical signalling of one link into another, letting a copper switch port reach a fiber run without replacing the switch. It does not route, NAT, or rewrite VLAN tags.

choices.text: It connects two different physical media, such as copper Ethernet to fiber
It translates private IPv4 addresses into public ones
It rewrites VLAN tags between two switches
It converts a Layer 3 packet into an Ethernet frame

stem: What is the role of a patch panel in structured cabling?
explanation: Horizontal cable is pulled once from the work area to the telecommunications room and terminated on the back of the patch panel. A short, easily replaced patch cord then connects the panel to the switch, so equipment can be moved without disturbing the building wiring.

choices.text: It terminates the permanent horizontal cable and provides a jack for a short patch cord to the switch
It regenerates the signal so runs can exceed 100 meters
It assigns IP addresses to the devices that connect to it
It converts copper links into fiber links

stem: Which capability distinguishes a managed switch from an unmanaged switch?
explanation: Both types learn MAC addresses and forward frames. A managed switch adds an interface for configuration and monitoring: VLANs, trunking, STP features, port security, QoS, and SNMP. An unmanaged switch is plug-and-play with no addressable control plane.

choices.text: Configurable VLANs, spanning tree, and per-port settings through a management interface
The ability to forward frames using MAC addresses
Multiple copper ports in one chassis
A metal chassis that fits a rack

stem: Using TCP at the transport layer, what are the PDU names at the transport, network, and data-link layers?
explanation: TCP hands down a segment, IP encapsulates it into a packet, and the data-link layer wraps that into a frame before the physical layer sends bits. Each layer adds its own header, and the receiver strips them in reverse order.

choices.text: Segment, packet, frame
Frame, packet, segment
Datagram, frame, bit
Packet, segment, frame

stem: Which OSI layer establishes, manages, and terminates dialogues between applications?
explanation: The session layer sets up, maintains, and tears down the conversation between two applications, including checkpointing and recovery. The transport layer moves data end to end, while the presentation layer handles formatting and encryption.

choices.text: Session layer (Layer 5)
Transport layer (Layer 4)
Presentation layer (Layer 6)
Application layer (Layer 7)

stem: Which OSI layer provides network services such as HTTP and DNS directly to user applications?
explanation: The application layer is the boundary the user's software talks to: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, and SSH live here. It does not move bytes itself; it hands data to the presentation and session layers below, which prepare and manage the exchange.

choices.text: Application layer (Layer 7)
Presentation layer (Layer 6)
Session layer (Layer 5)
Transport layer (Layer 4)

stem: Which OSI layers are combined into the TCP/IP application layer?
explanation: The TCP/IP model collapses the top three OSI layers into one application layer, because protocols such as HTTP and DNS handle their own formatting and session state. Transport maps to transport, and network maps to the internet layer, while data-link and physical map to the network access layer.

choices.text: Application, presentation, and session
Transport and network
Data-link and physical
Network, data-link, and physical

stem: Why is fiber optic cabling preferred in an industrial area with heavy electrical machinery?
explanation: Fiber carries modulated light through glass, so motors, welders, and power cables cannot induce noise onto the signal. It also provides electrical isolation between endpoints, which is why it is used on long runs between buildings with different ground potentials.

choices.text: Light in the fiber is unaffected by electromagnetic interference
The fiber's copper core cancels induced noise
The fiber carries a ground reference that absorbs surges
The fiber transmits at a lower voltage than copper

stem: What is the purpose of an SFP or SFP+ slot on a switch?
explanation: The slot holds a transceiver module that converts the switch's electrical signal to the media in use, such as multimode fiber, single-mode fiber, or a direct-attach copper cable. Changing the module changes the media without replacing the switch.

choices.text: It accepts a hot-swappable transceiver so the port can support different fiber or copper media
It supplies Power over Ethernet to attached devices
It stacks multiple switches into one management domain
It stores the switch's startup configuration

stem: Why is coaxial cable still used on the WAN side of a cable broadband connection?
explanation: Cable operators built their access networks on coaxial cable and reuse it with DOCSIS, which modulates Ethernet frames onto the coax spectrum. The modem converts between coax and the subscriber's Ethernet link, so the plant does not need to be replaced with fiber to deliver service.

choices.text: It carries the DOCSIS signal between the subscriber's modem and the provider's cable network
It provides a fiber path from the provider to the home
It is the required medium for all Ethernet WAN services
It removes the need for a cable modem

stem: Why does a twisted-pair Ethernet channel stop at about 100 meters?
explanation: The signal weakens as it travels, and near-end crosstalk from adjacent pairs grows relative to it. Beyond roughly 100 meters the signal-to-noise ratio falls below what the receiver needs at the standard data rate. That is a physical limit, not a forwarding rule.

choices.text: Attenuation and crosstalk grow with distance until the receiver can no longer separate the symbols
The copper oxidises once the cable passes 100 meters
Switches cannot forward a frame more than 100 meters
IEEE 802.3 caps the length to conserve IPv4 addresses

stem: Which device terminates many simultaneous remote-access VPN tunnels from mobile users?
explanation: A VPN concentrator is built for scale: hundreds or thousands of encrypted tunnels terminate on one appliance instead of on the router that also runs the WAN. It handles the crypto, the address pool, and per-user policy in one place, whereas a site-to-site tunnel is one link between two fixed peers.

choices.text: A VPN concentrator
A Layer 2 access switch
A media converter
A DHCP relay agent

stem: What does an explicit forward proxy provide for internal users browsing the internet?
explanation: Users point their browser at the proxy, and it makes the request on their behalf, so the remote site sees the proxy's address rather than the client's. That position lets it cache popular content, log requests, and block categories, and it keeps direct outbound connections off the desktop.

choices.text: It fetches content on the client's behalf, which hides the client address and enforces caching and filtering policy
It gives each internal host a public address through static NAT
It terminates IPsec tunnels from remote branch routers
It inspects only Layer 2 frames for malformed headers

stem: Which control is specific to a web application firewall rather than a stateful packet filter?
explanation: A WAF parses HTTP requests and responses, so it can reject an SQL injection string or a cross-site scripting payload inside a request that is otherwise a well-formed TCP connection to port 443. A port-based firewall permits that conversation because the ports and the handshake look normal.

choices.text: It examines HTTP requests and blocks injection and cross-site scripting payloads
It tracks TCP connection state to allow return traffic
It filters traffic by source and destination port number
It translates private addresses to public addresses

stem: A firewall is inserted inline in a subnet, has no IP address on its data interfaces, and requires no change to host default gateways. Which deployment mode is this?
explanation: In transparent (Layer 2) mode the firewall bridges the segment and filters on MAC and frame content, so the existing addressing plan is untouched. Its management interface still carries an address. Routed mode would require every host to point at the firewall as its gateway.

choices.text: Transparent Layer 2 mode
Routed Layer 3 mode
Tap (promiscuous) monitoring mode
Full proxy mode with per-host TLS interception

stem: Which flag combination begins an orderly TCP connection teardown by one side?
explanation: The closing host sends FIN to say it has no more data, the peer acknowledges with ACK, and each side repeats the exchange for its own direction. That is why a graceful close takes four segments, unlike the three-segment open. A RST would abort the connection instead.

choices.text: FIN, followed by an ACK from the peer
SYN, followed by SYN-ACK
RST, followed by a second RST
PSH, followed by URG

stem: Which port range is reserved for well-known services such as SSH and HTTP?
explanation: Ports 0 through 1023 are the well-known range, assigned to standard services and reachable without elevated privileges only by the system. Registered ports run from 1024 to 49151, and the ephemeral range above that is what a client picks as its source port.

stem: What uniquely identifies a single TCP conversation on a host that runs several applications at once?
explanation: A socket is the pairing of an IP address and a port, and a connection is the pairing of a source socket with a destination socket. Two browser tabs to the same server differ only in their ephemeral source ports, which is how the host keeps their data streams apart.

choices.text: The socket: an IP address plus a port number
The destination MAC address alone
The sequence number of the first segment
The VLAN identifier of the host's access port

stem: A developer needs a small Linux virtual machine on a Windows laptop for testing. Which hypervisor type fits that use case?
explanation: A Type 2 hypervisor installs as an application on the host operating system, so it shares the laptop's drivers and needs no dedicated hardware. A Type 1 hypervisor would take over the whole machine and is what a production server or a bare-metal lab host normally runs.

choices.text: A Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor installed on the desktop OS
A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor that replaces the desktop OS
A container runtime with no virtual machine involved
A VXLAN gateway on the physical switch

stem: What does live migration of a virtual machine accomplish?
explanation: The hypervisor copies the running VM's memory to the destination host while the VM keeps executing, then briefly pauses it to move the last dirty pages and switch execution. Because downtime is measured in milliseconds, maintenance on a host no longer requires an outage window.

choices.text: It moves a running VM to another host with only a brief pause, avoiding an outage for host maintenance
It converts a virtual machine into a container image
It clones a VM's disk to a backup repository on a schedule
It spreads one VM's CPU load across every host in the cluster

stem: Why do production container deployments rely on an orchestrator rather than starting containers by hand?
explanation: An orchestrator holds the desired state: how many replicas, which image, which network, which health check. When a container dies or a node fails it schedules a replacement, and it spreads replicas across hosts. Doing that manually does not scale past a handful of containers.

choices.text: It maintains the declared replica count, reschedules failed containers, and places them across hosts
It compiles the application source into a container image
It replaces the need for a container registry
It provides the kernel that every container shares

stem: What is the role of a container registry?
explanation: Images are built once, pushed to a registry, and pulled by every host or orchestrator that needs to run them. The registry is versioned storage, not a runtime: the container still needs a local engine to unpack and start the image after the pull.

choices.text: It stores and versions container images so hosts can pull them
It runs the containers on behalf of the cluster
It allocates the IP addresses used inside the container network
It converts container images into virtual machine disks

stem: What problem does SD-WAN solve that a traditional set of static WAN circuits does not?
explanation: SD-WAN applies a central policy to all transports and picks a path per application, so a video call can ride the low-latency link while bulk backup uses a cheaper one. When a circuit degrades, traffic moves to another transport without reconfiguring each router by hand.

choices.text: It steers each application over the best available transport and fails over between links from a central policy
It replaces IP routing with Layer 2 switching across the provider network
It guarantees a fixed committed rate on every internet circuit
It removes the need for encryption on links that cross the internet

stem: Which characteristic distinguishes a leased line from a broadband internet circuit?
explanation: A leased line is a dedicated, symmetric circuit with a committed rate and an SLA, and it does not share capacity with other subscribers. Broadband is oversubscribed and usually asymmetric, which is why it costs less but gives no performance guarantee.

choices.text: It is a dedicated symmetric circuit with a committed rate and an SLA
It shares provider capacity with other subscribers and has no SLA
It is always encrypted by the provider at Layer 2
It provides internet access only, never site-to-site connectivity

stem: A provider offers a Metro Ethernet E-Line service between two sites. What does the customer receive?
explanation: E-Line is a point-to-point Ethernet virtual circuit, so the two sites behave as if a cable ran between them. E-LAN is the multipoint service that lets many sites share one bridged domain, and E-Tree is the hub-and-spoke variant.

choices.text: A point-to-point Ethernet virtual circuit between the two locations
A multipoint bridged domain shared by every site
A Layer 3 MPLS VPN with any-to-any routing
A dedicated internet gateway with a public address block

stem: What is the demarcation point at a customer site?
explanation: The demarc is where the provider's responsibility ends and the customer's begins, usually the smart jack or the first device the carrier owns. Knowing where it sits settles who must troubleshoot a circuit that will not come up.

choices.text: The boundary where the service provider's responsibility ends and the customer's begins
The point where the internal network connects to the DMZ switch
The router's loopback interface used for management
The first hop router inside the provider's core

stem: An access point runs its entire configuration locally and has no controller. Which deployment model is this?
explanation: An autonomous AP is self-contained: it holds its own SSIDs, security, and channel settings, so each AP must be configured and upgraded individually. A lightweight AP holds almost no configuration and receives it from a WLC, which is what makes central management possible.

choices.text: Autonomous AP deployment
Lightweight AP deployment managed by a WLC
FlexConnect deployment with local switching
Cloud-managed AP deployment

stem: What does Radio Resource Management (RRM) do on a Cisco wireless controller?
explanation: RRM collects interference and load measurements from the APs and then adjusts channel assignments and transmit power automatically. That keeps neighbouring APs from sitting on the same channel and prevents coverage holes when an AP fails, without an engineer retuning the deployment.

choices.text: It dynamically adjusts AP channels and transmit power based on measured interference and load
It assigns IP addresses to wireless clients through DHCP
It authenticates clients against a RADIUS server
It encrypts CAPWAP control traffic between APs and the controller

stem: Why is a guest WLAN often tunnelled to an anchor controller in the DMZ?
explanation: Guest traffic must leave the network without touching internal subnets. Tunnelling it from the foreign controller to an anchor in the DMZ means the guest client's VLAN and its egress point both sit outside the internal firewall policy, so a guest cannot reach internal resources by accident.

choices.text: So guest traffic exits through the DMZ instead of entering internal subnets
So guest clients receive addresses from the internal DHCP scope
So guest traffic can be bridged directly onto the internal VLAN
So the anchor controller can manage the APs' radio settings

stem: An AP sits on a subnet with no broadcast path to the wireless controller. How does it learn the controller's address?
explanation: DHCP option 43 carries the controller's address in the lease, so the AP does not need broadcast or a DNS alias to find it. The AP then sends a discovery request unicast to that address. Without the option, the AP would have to rely on a configured DNS name or a static entry.

choices.text: The DHCP server returns the controller address in option 43
The AP floods a broadcast on the voice VLAN and waits for a reply
The switch pushes the address to the AP through CDP
The AP derives the address from its own default gateway

stem: Which access method must an 802.11 station use before it transmits a frame?
explanation: Wireless is a shared medium, so a station must sense the channel and wait a random backoff before sending, then wait for an acknowledgement. Collisions are detected by the missing ACK rather than by listening while transmitting, which is why the method is collision avoidance.

choices.text: Carrier sense with a random backoff, then an acknowledgement from the receiver
A token that circulates between stations in sequence
A reservation slot requested from the access point for every frame
Immediate transmission, with collisions resolved by a retry timer

stem: Two clients can each hear the AP but not each other, so their transmissions collide at the AP. Which mechanism mitigates this hidden node problem?
explanation: A hidden node cannot sense the other client's carrier, so it transmits whenever the channel looks idle. If the AP first sends a clear-to-send frame that reserves the medium, both clients hear it and hold off, which is why RTS/CTS is enabled in cells with hidden nodes.

choices.text: Request-to-send and clear-to-send frames that reserve the medium
A longer preamble on every beacon frame
Switching the cell to a 40 MHz channel
Increasing the AP's transmit power only

stem: What information does an 802.11 beacon frame carry to clients?
explanation: Beacons are broadcast at a fixed interval and advertise the SSID, supported rates, security settings, and channel so a client can discover the cell and decide whether it can join. A client that receives no beacon can still probe actively, but the beacon is what makes passive discovery work.

choices.text: The SSID, supported data rates, security settings, and channel of the cell
The client's IP address and default gateway
The controller's management address and licence count
The MAC addresses of every client currently associated

stem: Place these steps in the order a client follows when joining a wireless network: authentication, association, 802.11 authentication, discovery.
explanation: The client first discovers the cell through a beacon or probe response, then completes the open 802.11 authentication exchange, then associates so the AP creates a state entry for it. Only after association can the stronger security exchange and DHCP occur.

choices.text: Discovery, 802.11 authentication, association
Association, discovery, 802.11 authentication
802.11 authentication, discovery, association
Discovery, association, 802.11 authentication

stem: Which 802.11 amendment operates in the 2.4 GHz band at a maximum rate of 11 Mbps?
explanation: 802.11b introduced 11 Mbps in the crowded 2.4 GHz band using DSSS, and its 1, 6, and 11 Mbps rates were enough to make wireless practical. 802.11a offered 54 Mbps later but only in 5 GHz, and 802.11g brought 54 Mbps to 2.4 GHz.

stem: Which capability did 802.11n add that earlier amendments did not have?
explanation: 802.11n was the first amendment to define operation in both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, and it added MIMO and optional 40 MHz channels. Running in either band let a client use the cleaner 5 GHz spectrum while older devices stayed on 2.4 GHz.

choices.text: Operation in both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands with MIMO and 40 MHz channels
The 6 GHz band and orthogonal frequency-division multiple access
A 160 MHz channel width in the 5 GHz band only
Multi-user MIMO with eight spatial streams in 2.4 GHz

stem: Which band does 802.11ac use, and how is it marketed?
